metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz and doubles partner Jakub Mensik gave Team Europe a 3-1 lead over Team World after the opening day of the Laver Cup on Friday.

Alcaraz and Mensik beat Alexander Bublik and Taylor Fritz 6-4 6-4 in the final match of the day at the O2 Arena in London. Rafael Jodar had broken a 1-1 deadlock after the day session by defeating Bublik 6-2 6-3 in the evening's singles match. In the day session, Brandon Nakashima made the most of his Laver Cup debut by beating Mensik 6-1 3-6 10-7. In the event's opener, Casper Ruud beat Francisco Cerundolo 6-7 (4-7) 6-4 10-8 to give Europe an early lead. There are four matches per day in the three-day event. messages.text: Warrington reach Grand Final after penalty drama and Leeds' last-kick miss

metadata.summary: Warrington Wolves made it through to the Super League Grand Final with a 14-12 victory over Leeds Rhinos, a controversial penalty proving the difference at Headingley Stadium.
metadata.content: Warrington Wolves through to Super League Grand Final after controversial penalty with 14-12 win over Leeds Rhinos | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Warrington Wolves through to Super League Grand Final after controversial penalty with 14-12 win over Leeds Rhinos Warrington Wolves are into the Grand Final for the first time since 2018; The two points came from a penalty for an escort on George Williams; The play-offs are under way, live on Sky Sports, and continue through until the Grand Final from Old Trafford on October 3 Friday 25 September 2026 23:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Super League semi-final clash between Leeds Rhinos and Warrington Wolves. Warrington Wolves made it through to the Super League Grand Final with a 14-12 victory over Leeds Rhinos, a controversial penalty proving the difference at Headingley Stadium. It marks Warrington's first Grand Final since 2018 and they have never been victors in the big dance before. Leeds, meanwhile, are left waiting once again, with their last Grand Final victory coming all the way back in 2017. The flashpoint of the match came in the 66th minute when James McDonnell was pinged for an escort on George Williams. It appeared as though Williams had potentially run into the Leeds man's line, but despite the Rhinos using their Captain's Challenge the decision was upheld and Ewan Irwin sent over the conversion to win the game. Palmer was a controversial omission from England's World Cup squad in the summer, with an injury-hit season impacting his form. After a summer off, it appeared Palmer was returning to a high level in the early weeks of this campaign, with six goal involvements in seven games for Chelsea. That output earned him a recall to the England group for the Nations League matches with Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia - but Palmer withdrew from the squad due to injury. messages.text: Hain leads Warwickshire's bid for title-clinching win over Leicestershire

metadata.summary: Sam Hain struck a superb 142 to nudge Warwickshire closer to the Rothesay County Championship title as they lead Leicestershire by 192 runs at Edgbaston at the end of day two.
metadata.content: County Championship: Sam Hain leads Warwickshire's bid for title-clinching win over Leicestershire at Edgbaston | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Sam Hain leads Warwickshire's bid for title-clinching win over Leicestershire at Edgbaston Friday's County Championship sees Warwickshire move ever closer to title after moving into lead of 192 runs against relegation-threatened Leicestershire at Edgbaston at the end of day two; Warwickshire win would guarantee a first title since the Covid-shortened 2021 campaign Friday 25 September 2026 20:22, UK Image: Sam Hain produced 142 with the bat to push Warwickshire ever closer to the County Championship title Sam Hain struck a superb 142 to nudge Warwickshire closer to the Rothesay County Championship title as they lead Leicestershire by 192 runs at Edgbaston at the end of day two. Warwickshire needed at least 14 points from their final match of the season and have already taken six bonus points after skittling Leicestershire for 125 on day one before Hain led the home side to 372 all out in reply. Leicestershire, who slipped to 55-3 in their second innings at close, are all but relegated, subject to their appeal against a 27-point deduction for a substandard pitch at Grace Road last month. Second-placed Somerset's title hopes appear over - they began their last fixture 11 points behind Warwickshire - even if they beat Surrey at Taunton. The United States have never been beaten on home soil in the biennial contest and have won 13 of the previous 15 editions, although now find themselves behind after an impressive Friday performance from Geoff Ogilvy's International Team at Medinah. Canadian duo Corey Conners and Nick Taylor held off world No 1 Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns to claim a 1up win in the top match, having already seen Hideki Matsuyama and Sungjae Im despatch Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman 3&2.
